fact: The Bank of Tanzania's Cloud Computing Guidelines for Financial Service Providers, 2025 (issued under s.71 Banking and Financial Institutions Act 2006 and s.56(3) National Payment Systems Act 2015) bar a licensed financial service provider from hosting a mission-critical system, or one whose data the Bank deems critical, in a primary data centre or cloud whose hosting infrastructure is outside Tanzania; the document is dated August 2025.
system: Cloud Computing Guidelines for Financial Service Providers, 2025

fact: The guidelines make the Bank of Tanzania the body that evaluates and approves financial service providers' cloud arrangements and contracts, and say it may impose sanctions including civil money penalties for contravention.

fact: Paragraph 8 of the Cybercrimes (Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure) Order, 2026 (GN 147, 19 June 2026) requires owners of critical information infrastructure to host all related data within the United Republic, and to seek the Minister's approval to host primary or secondary data outside it.
system: Cybercrimes (Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure) Order, 2026

fact: The Order makes the Minister the approver of offshore hosting of critical infrastructure data and has the Ministry responsible for ICT keep the register, receive reports and audit and inspect the infrastructure at least annually.
